findings.title: Dereference of undefined destination calendar for Google Meet fallback
findings.body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array (now a valid state and produced by several callers), destructuring yields `undefined`, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. Creating any event with `location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar throws before bookings/emails are created. Use optional chaining or check for a destination before reading `.integration`.

findings.title: Video meeting references lose credentialId
findings.body: For non-calendar results (`isCalendarType` false), the new code sets `credentialId: undefined`; previously it preserved `result.credentialId`. Video meeting creation returns a credential id, and downstream cancellation code only deletes a video reference when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so video meetings can be left behind on cancellation/reschedule. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results.

findings.title: Location updates create calendar references without calendar linkage
findings.body: `updateLocation` now builds references from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not populate either field (it returns only appName/type/success/uid/updatedEvent/originalEvent/calError/calWarnings). Every location edit therefore creates calendar references with null `credentialId` and `externalCalendarId`, so later cancellation/reschedule can target the wrong calendar or all credentials. Populate these fields in updateEvent or derive them from the destination calendar.

findings.title: Stale credential reused when a multi-host credential lookup fails
findings.body: Inside the new loop over calendar references, `credential` is declared outside the loop and only overwritten when the in-memory or DB lookup succeeds. If a later reference's credential is missing, `credential` still holds the previous reference's credential and is passed to `updateEvent` with the current reference's uid/externalCalendarId, potentially updating the wrong calendar. Reset/skip when no credential is found.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: The PR now supports multiple calendar references, but the `newBookingId` merge branch still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only one old calendar event. Collective bookings can have references for several hosts, so old events for all but the first host remain on their calendars after a reschedule/merge. Iterate over all calendar references when deleting old events.

findings.title: Google Calendar fallback compares externalId to a null externalCalendarId
findings.body: In `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy the code does `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, i.e. compares calendar ids to null/undefined. That never matches. `updateEvent` then calls Google with an undefined calendarId and `deleteEvent` falls back to `primary`, so events on a non-primary destination calendar are updated/deleted on the wrong calendar or fail. Use the matching destination for the current credential, or at least the first destination, when no external id is supplied.

findings.title: Google insert patches hangout link with undefined calendarId
findings.body: The insert call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary'`, but the subsequent hangout-link patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. When no destination calendar matches the credential, the event is created on primary but the patch is sent with an undefined calendarId, so the hangout link/description is not patched and the unawaited call can reject. Use the same fallback for both calls.

findings.title: Collective co-host calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so destination calendars collected from co-hosts are discarded. A collective host with a calendar will not get an event if the organizer has none. Initialize to `[]` before pushing.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: EventManager calls createEvent once per destination credential, but Office365's createEvent reads `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and uses that calendar for every call. With two Office365 hosts, both calls create the event on the first host's calendar (or fail for the second credential), so additional hosts never get the event and the first can get duplicates. Select the destination belonging to the current credential (pass credentialId/externalId) instead of index 0.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: Lark's createEvent derives the calendar id from `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. EventManager invokes the service for each destination credential, so a second Lark host's event is created against the first host's calendar id, likely failing due to permissions or writing into the wrong calendar. Use the destination matching the current credential rather than the first array entry.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent filters all calendars by the first destination
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters calendars using only `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. When a collective booking has multiple CalDAV destinations, every invocation filters to that first calendar, so other hosts' calendars never receive an event and the first calendar can receive duplicates. Select the destination for the current credential or pass the target externalId into createEvent.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation ignores non-organizer credentials
findings.body: The outer loop now iterates every calendar reference, but the recurring cancellation branch still builds its work from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and picks the first calendar reference per updated booking. Co-hosts' credentials are not in the organizer's `credentials`, and their per-reference ids are ignored, so recurring collective bookings leave calendar events on co-host calendars. Delete using each reference's own credential/external id.

findings.title: Organization slug logic is inverted
findings.body: This unrelated change flips `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. With billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are now created without a slug; with billing enabled, both `slug` and `requestedSlug` are set before domain verification. Restore the original conditions unless this behavior change is intentional and covered.
